texto: The system must allow visitors and customers to enter the virtual store and browse the main catalog.
The system must organize products by animal categories, including fish, dogs, reptiles, cats, and birds.
The system must allow access to categories through different navigation paths, such as the main menu, quick shortcuts, and visual elements on the home page.
The system must allow viewing the product list of each category.
The system must allow viewing the available items of each product.
The system must allow viewing item details, including description, identifier, price, and stock status.
The system must allow searching products by keyword.
The search must consider the product name as the basis for returning results.
When no keyword is provided, the system must block the search and guide the user to fill in the search field.
The system must maintain the catalog as a separate capability, responsible for products, categories, items, and search.
The catalog capability depends on inventory to provide updated stock information for items.
The system must allow registering new customers by filling in identification, contact, address, and access credential data.
The system must allow customers to authenticate using username and password.
The system must inform when authentication cannot be completed due to invalid username or password.
The system must allow customers to end their usage session.
The system must allow customers to edit their registration data and profile preferences.
The system must allow customers to define their preferred language.
The system must allow customers to choose a favorite category.
The system must allow customers to enable a personalized product list based on their favorite category.
The system must allow customers to enable a promotional banner related to their favorite category.
The system must reflect customer preferences, such as the personalized list and banner associated with the favorite category.
The system must maintain the customer account as a separate capability, responsible for registration, profile, and preferences.
The system must maintain authentication as a capability separate from the customer account, responsible for login, session, and access control.
The customer account capability depends on authentication to validate user access.
The system must allow adding items to the shopping cart from product pages and item detail pages.
When the same item is added more than once, the system must consolidate the item in the cart and increase its quantity.
The system must allow viewing the cart with selected items, quantities, unit prices, and totals by item.
The system must inform, for each cart item, whether it is available in stock at the time of inclusion.
The system must allow updating item quantities in the cart.
The system must allow removing items from the cart.
When the informed quantity for an item is less than 1, the system must remove it from the cart.
The system must automatically calculate the cart subtotal based on selected items and quantities.
The system must maintain the cart as a separate capability, responsible for the temporary selection of items.
The shopping cart capability depends on the catalog to identify the selected items.
The shopping cart capability depends on inventory to validate item availability.
The system must inform stock availability when viewing an item.
When there is no available quantity in stock, the system must indicate that the item is on backorder.
The system must consult stock status in an updated manner at critical points of the purchase journey.
When completing an order, the system must register the decrease of the purchased quantity from stock.
The system must maintain inventory as a separate capability, responsible for item availability and stock decrease.
The inventory capability depends on the catalog to identify the items whose stock is being managed.
The system must require the user to be authenticated to start the checkout process.
When starting an order, the system must use the customer registration data to initially fill in billing and delivery information.
The system must use the cart items to automatically compose the order.
The system must allow customers to inform or adjust order payment data.
The system must allow choosing the card type among the options available in the application.
The system must allow customers to indicate a delivery address different from the billing address.
When the customer chooses a different delivery address, the system must present a specific step for filling in that address.
Before finalization, the system must present a confirmation step with the informed billing and delivery data.
The system must complete the order only after explicit customer confirmation.
When completing the order, the system must generate a unique purchase identifier.
When completing the order, the system must record the purchase date, acquired items, quantities, values, and initial order status.
After purchase completion, the system must clear the customer cart.
After purchase completion, the system must display a confirmation message for order receipt.
The system must maintain the order as a separate capability, responsible for checkout and order lifecycle.
The order capability depends on authentication to validate access.
The order capability depends on the customer account to obtain registration data.
The order capability depends on the shopping cart to obtain the items being purchased.
The order capability depends on inventory to register the stock decrease.
The system must allow customers to consult their list of completed orders.
The order listing must show at least order number, date, and total value.
The system must allow consulting the details of a specific order.
The order details must show payment data, addresses, carrier, status, purchased items, quantities, prices, and total purchase value.
The system must restrict order viewing to the respective customer responsible for the purchase.
The system must protect checkout and order consultation features through customer authentication.
The system must properly end the customer session at logout, avoiding continued unauthorized authenticated access.
The system must not unnecessarily expose the customer password during navigation after login.
The system must maintain consistency among cart, order, and inventory, avoiding divergences between the completed purchase and registered items.
The system must ensure that the order is registered with all main elements, including header, status, and purchased items.
The system must ensure uniqueness in order numbering, allowing purchase traceability.
The system must automatically calculate cart and order values, reducing manual error risk.
The system must handle invalid inputs in a controlled way, displaying appropriate messages without compromising application continuity.
The system must prevent inconsistent operations, such as starting checkout without authentication or silently manipulating nonexistent items.
The system must preserve order history for later customer consultation.
The system must offer simple and understandable navigation, with clear access to categories, search, cart, customer account, and help.
The purchase process must be conducted in logical and progressive steps, making checkout easier to understand.
The system must provide guidance and confirmation messages at important flow points, such as login failure, empty search field, and completed order.
